newsitem.title: USA: BTG wins Army contract, shares leap.
newsitem.headline: BTG wins Army contract, shares leap.

text.p: BTG Inc said Friday it was one of two companies awarded a $554 million U.S. Army contract to provide advanced personal computers, related hardware and software.
A company spokesman said BTG expects the new business to result in an order backlog of $200 million over two years.
For fiscal 1996, ended in March, BTG reported revenues of $214 million and net income of almost $3 million, or $0.47 per share.
In unusually active Nasdaq trade BTG rose to 17-7/8, a new year high, from 15, then eased back to 17, up two.
Shortly before midday, more than 216,000 shares had changed hands, well above the average daily volume of about 34,000.
The BTG spokesman said the contract is an "indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity" pact and allows BTG to market its products to different parts of the Army.

The Army will acquire commercial off-the-shelf personal computers with performance levels equal to either a Pentium 166 MHz or Pentium Pro 200, and BTG will provide warranty service on the PCs and offer a variety of operating systems, hard disk drives, color monitors, software and related items, the company said.
